R Notebook

Lab | Data Wrangling with R

Objective

Practice data wrangling, cleaning, and manipulation techniques in R using the Sample Super Store dataset. By the end of this activity, you should be able to:

  • Load and explore the dataset.

  • Perform basic and advanced data manipulations.

  • Handle missing data and duplicates.

  • Aggregate and summarize data.

  • Dataset Overview.

The Sample Super Store dataset contains sales, profit, and customer information for a retail store. It includes columns such as:

  • Order ID, Order Date, Ship Date

  • Customer ID, Customer Name, Segment

  • City, State, Region, Category, Sub-Category

  • Sales, Quantity, Discount, Profit

Instructions

Step 1: Load and Explore the Dataset

  1. Load the dataset into R.

  2. Explore the dataset using str(), head(), and summary().

  3. Identify the number of rows and columns.

```r
superstore <- read.csv("Sample - Superstore.csv")
head(superstore)
```

Step 2: Basic Data Manipulation

  1. Select the following columns: Order ID, Order Date, Customer Name, Sales, Profit.

  2. Filter the dataset to show only orders with a profit greater than $100.

  3. Sort the dataset by Sales in descending order.

```r
library(dplyr)
order_cust_sales <- superstore[c("Order.ID", "Order.Date", "Customer.Name", "Sales", "Profit")]
order_cust_sales <- filter(order_cust_sales, Profit > 1000)
order_cust_sales <- order_cust_sales %>% arrange(desc(Sales))
order_cust_sales
```

Step 3: Handle Missing Data

  1. Check for missing values in the dataset.

  2. Replace missing values in the Postal Code column with the mode (most frequent value).

  3. Remove rows with missing values in the Customer Name column.

```r
colSums(is.na(superstore))
```
```
       Row.ID      Order.ID    Order.Date     Ship.Date     Ship.Mode   Customer.ID Customer.Name       Segment       Country          City         State   Postal.Code        Region    Product.ID

```

Step 4: Create and Modify Columns

  1. Create a new column Profit_Margin as the ratio of Profit to Sales.

  2. Create a new column Order_Year by extracting the year from Order Date.

  3. Convert the Order.Date column to a Date data type.

```r
superstore <- transform(superstore, Profit_Margin = Profit / Sales)
superstore$Order.Date <- as.Date(superstore$Order.Date, format = "%d/%m/%Y")
superstore$Year <- format(superstore$Order.Date, "%Y" )
superstore
```

Step 5: Aggregating and Summarizing Data

  1. Calculate the total sales and profit by Category.
```r
library(dplyr)
category_sales <- superstore %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Sales = sum(Sales, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Profit = sum(Profit, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(category_sales)
```

  1. Find the average profit margin by Region.
```r
region_margin <- superstore %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  summarise(
    Avg_profit = mean(Profit)
  )
region_margin
```

  group_by(Segment) %>%
  count(Segment, name = "number of Orderd")

  1. Create a new column Discount_Level that categorizes discounts as “Low” (<10%), “Medium” (10-20%), and “High” (>20%).
```r
superstore <- superstore %>%
  mutate(Discount_Level = case_when(
                      Discount >= 0  & Discount < 0.1 ~ "Low",
                      Discount >= 0.1  & Discount <= 0.2 ~ "Medium",
                      Discount > 0.2  & Discount <= 1 ~ "High",
                      TRUE ~ NA_character_
                    ))
```
  1. Merge the dataset with a new dataset containing regional population data (create a dummy dataset for this purpose).
```r
# Create a dummy dataset to join
region_data <- data.frame(
  Region = c("East", "West", "Central", "South"),
  Population = c(5000000, 3000000, 4000000, 3500000)
)

superstore <- superstore %>%
    left_join(region_data, by = "Region")
```

Extra 2: Data Visualization

Next class we will talk about data visualization, but let’s see if you can pull it off on your own.

  1. Create a bar plot of total sales by Category.
```r
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(category_sales, aes(x = Category, y = Total_Sales)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Total Sales by Category", x = "Category", y = "Total Sales") +
  theme_minimal()
```

  1. Create a scatter plot of Sales vs. Profit with a trend line.
```r
ggplot(superstore, aes(x = Sales, y = Profit)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +  # Точки
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +  # Линия тренда
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot of Sales vs. Profit with Trend Line", 
       x = "Sales", y = "Profit") +
  theme_minimal()
```

  1. Create a histogram of Profit_Margin.
```r
ggplot(superstore, aes(x = Profit.Margin)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Profit Margin", x = "Profit Margin", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
```
